title: Make the fake host keep the promises QMUX keeps

blocks.text: The payments team tests its clients against `ScriptedMux`, a stand-in host in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ScriptedMux.java`. A test scripts the next answers with `then(...)`: a response code such as `"00"` or `"51"`, or `ScriptedMux.SILENT` for a host that says nothing. Once the script runs out, the host approves.

Last month two bugs reached production although tests had been written for both. A client that sent every unanswered authorization a second time passed the test that was meant to catch it, and a client that kept the 0100 it sent, to build a reversal from it later, found an 0110 there instead. Both times the fake was the culprit, and its answering part is now blank.

Finish the three methods marked `TODO`: both forms of `request`, and `answer`, which builds the response. When you're done, a client tested against `ScriptedMux` meets the same behaviour it will meet behind a real QMUX, for authorizations, reversals and anything else it sends. About a dozen lines in total.

cases.says: each request gets the scripted answer in order, a silent step gives null, and after the script every request is approved
the listener form hands an answered request's response to responseReceived with the hand-back
a request the host left unanswered is still recorded as sent, so a test can tell a resend from a single attempt
the response is a new message and the client's request is left unchanged, as with QMUX
the response MTI is derived from the request's: an 0100 is answered by an 0110 and an 0420 by an 0430
with no answer the listener form calls expired once and never passes null to responseReceived
the response echoes the request's fields, as a host's answer does, besides adding field 39

origin.section: 10.1.1 Spot the Problem: The Fake That Answered With the Request

concepts: A fake MUX lets a test decide every answer, and it must answer as QMUX does: a new message with the response MTI and the request's fields, null for silence, expired on the listener form, and a record of everything sent.
